title: R_4(2(x-y)=3z) = 226
statement: The 4-colour Rado number of the equation 2(x-y) = 3z is exactly 226: every 4-colouring of {1,...,226} contains a monochromatic solution, and some 4-colouring of {1,...,225} avoids one. This settles the only non-exact entry (previously '> 225') in Table 10 of Chang-De Loera-Wesley (2022).

notes: New result: settles the open Table 10 entry. The equation sits in the 'formula-free band' a = b+-1: the sequence R_1..R_4 = 4, 13, 61, 226 admits no constant-coefficient linear recurrence (difference-ratios 16/3 and 55/16 differ), unlike the a=1 family where R_k(x-y=2z) = (2*4^k+1)/3 fits all known values. Curiosity: 226 - 1 = 225 = (b(a+b))^2, unsupported by the rest of the table. Trust doctrine: the product proof must come from axeyum's own stack; external solvers and checkers appear only in the oracle-corroboration role that ADR-0002 assigns them.
